name: S.C. Code 48-1-95 Wastewater utilities; procedures for significant spills
legal_basis: 48-1-95 (2012 Act No. 109; 2026 Act No. 146 renamed the agency)
status_reason: Public-notice duty: utilities must give public notice of a significant spill (5,000 gallons or more of untreated or partially treated domestic sewage) within 24 hours of discovery; DES gives notice if the utility does not. No channel named.
notes: (A)(5) "significant spill" = "a net discharge from a wastewater utility of at least five thousand gallons of untreated or partially treated domestic sewage", excluding spills from natural disasters, direct acts of a third party or other acts of God. (B) "Utilities must verbally notify the department of any significant spill within twenty-four hours"; written within five days. (E) "The department shall require that all wastewater utilities provide public notice of any significant spill of five thousand gallons or more within twenty-four hours of the discovery." "Where the responsible wastewater utility does not provide this notice ... the department shall provide public notice of the significant spill."

name: SC DES sewer system overflow reporting (Satellite Sewer System Program forms; SSO compliance and enforcement document)
operator: South Carolina Department of Environmental Services (formerly DHEC)
status_reason: Since 1998 DES requires reporting of any SSO reaching state waters, any over about 500 gallons not reaching water, and any that may cause a health or environmental concern; public notification programs required for 5,000 gallons or more since July 2008 (per DES document and City of Florence). Reports go on a mailed or faxed form; no public list found. DES is said to receive about 600 reported overflows a year.
notes: The 2021 SSO compliance document at dhec.sc.gov returned HTTP 503.

name: SC DES SSO report records (internal)
status_reason: No public table, map or download of SSO reports found (searched DES site, DES ArcGIS server folders water, Hosted, Emergency_Response, and ArcGIS Online). Records request is the only route.

name: SC DES Beach Monitoring: beach stations with advisory status (BW_Monitoring_Stations layer 0) and S.C. Beach Access Guide
operator: SC DES Bureau of Water, Aquatic Science
access_detail: https://gis.des.sc.gov/gisserver/rest/services/water/BW_Monitoring_Stations/MapServer/0/query?where=1%3D1&outFields=*&f=json: 123 stations on 2026-11-03 (102 No Advisory, 21 Long-Term). Public map https://gis.des.sc.gov/beachaccess/ (also old gis.dhec.sc.gov). Short-term advisories run one to two days; long-term are reassessed yearly.
status_reason: Machine-readable current advisory per beach station (No Advisory / Long-Term; short-term advisories in season May 1 to Oct 1). Snapshot to keep history.
